result.summary: The intersection provides basic pedestrian infrastructure including sidewalks and curb ramps, but lacks dedicated pedestrian signals at a signalized crossing. The environment is dominated by asphalt with minimal buffers between pedestrians and moving traffic.

hazards.name: Visual obstruction from parked vehicle
hazards.description: A vehicle parked very close to the intersection corner limits the sightlines between pedestrians and approaching drivers.

hazards.name: Lack of pedestrian signals
hazards.description: The intersection is signalized for vehicles, but no pedestrian-specific signals are visible to guide safe crossing.

interventions.title: Install Pedestrian Countdown Signals
interventions.description: Add dedicated pedestrian signal heads with countdown timers to provide clear crossing information.

interventions.title: Curb Extensions (Bulb-outs)
interventions.description: Extend the sidewalk into the parking lane to shorten the crossing distance and improve visibility between drivers and pedestrians.

interventions.title: Intersection Daylighting
interventions.description: Remove parking spaces immediately adjacent to the crosswalk to ensure clear sightlines.

result.summary: The pedestrian environment features basic sidewalks and a marked crosswalk but lacks physical protection or traffic calming measures. The presence of parked vehicles near the intersection and the absence of signals or stop signs increase the risk of vehicle-pedestrian conflicts.

hazards.name: Parked vehicle obstruction
hazards.description: A white SUV is parked close to the intersection, potentially blocking sightlines between drivers and pedestrians.
hazards.location_in_image: Right side of the image near the building corner.

hazards.name: Absence of traffic control
hazards.description: The intersection lacks visible stop signs or traffic signals to regulate vehicle flow and protect crossing pedestrians.

interventions.title: Curb Extensions
interventions.description: Install bulb-outs at the corners to shorten crossing distances and prevent vehicles from parking too close to the crosswalk.

interventions.title: High-Visibility Crosswalk
interventions.description: Upgrade the existing parallel-line crosswalk to a continental or ladder pattern to improve visibility for approaching drivers.

interventions.title: Street Trees
interventions.description: Add street trees along the sidewalk to provide a physical buffer and create vertical friction to naturally slow traffic.

result.summary: The intersection features a high-visibility marked crosswalk with a small pedestrian refuge island. While basic infrastructure like sidewalks and traffic signals are present, the wide roadway and lack of significant buffers or traffic calming measures create a car-oriented environment.

hazards.name: Long Crossing Distance
hazards.description: The wide roadway increases the time pedestrians are exposed to vehicle traffic.
hazards.location_in_image: Across the main roadway at the marked crosswalk.

hazards.name: Lack of Pedestrian Buffer
hazards.description: Minimal physical separation between the sidewalk and moving traffic.

interventions.title: Curb Extensions
interventions.description: Install bulb-outs at the corners to shorten the crossing distance and improve visibility.

interventions.title: Street Trees and Landscaping
interventions.description: Add street trees to provide a vertical buffer and encourage slower driving speeds.

result.summary: The pedestrian environment features a marked crosswalk on a mixed-use urban street, but safety is compromised by significant visual obstructions from parked vehicles. The sidewalk is narrow and partially obstructed by building stoops, and there is a lack of pedestrian-specific infrastructure like signals or curb extensions.

hazards.name: Visual Obstruction from Parked Vehicles
hazards.description: Parked cars are situated immediately adjacent to the crosswalk, blocking sightlines between drivers and pedestrians waiting to cross.
hazards.location_in_image: Right side of the street, along the curb line leading to the crosswalk.

hazards.name: Narrow Sidewalk with Obstructions
hazards.description: The sidewalk is narrow and further constrained by building stairs, making it difficult for multiple pedestrians or those with mobility aids to pass.
hazards.location_in_image: Right side of the image, in front of the row houses.

interventions.title: Curb Extensions (Bulb-outs)
interventions.description: Extend the sidewalk into the parking lane at the crosswalk to improve pedestrian visibility and reduce crossing distance.

interventions.title: Daylighting
interventions.description: Remove parking spaces closest to the crosswalk to ensure clear sightlines for both pedestrians and drivers.
